The prompt's HARD CONSTRAINT line tells Haiku 'the picked product's
name MUST contain ALL of these qualifier words'. Haiku occasionally
ignores this with long shortlists or when word-similarity is
tempting. Observed: 'Finish Quantum Ultimate 38 tabs' → 'Rexona Men
Deodorant 48hr Aerosol Quantum' — Haiku locked onto 'Quantum'
appearing in both and ignored that the deodorant lacks 'Ultimate'.

path". #444 disproved this empirically: deleting the stable .mlmodelc and

passed individually to GetContainerExtraConfigures, producing one

the runtime to the last value, so the container only saw one GPU even

once per type so all GPU UUIDs are joined

only diagnosed compose-managed services and missed cloudflared

fix(telegram): yield to event loop each poll iteration

httpx.MockTransport (and any synchronously-resolving transport) lets the
poll loop spin without ever yielding back to asyncio. That starves
`wait_for` timers and the `stop()` event check sequence - the
adapter loop appeared to run forever from the event loop's POV. Adding
`await asyncio.sleep(0)` per iteration restores fair scheduling.

In production this is a no-op overhead; real Telegram long-poll already
yields inside the httpx request.

feat(delegation): parent-pid watchdog in codeg-mcp

codeg-mcp is a grandchild of codeg / codeg-server (the agent CLI is the
intermediate). Windows doesn't propagate parent death to descendants
automatically, and a hung agent CLI on any platform can swallow the
stdin EOF that would otherwise let codeg-mcp exit, both leaving the
companion alive indefinitely and holding the binary file locked.

- New cross-platform parent_watcher module: liveness probe via
  libc::kill(pid, 0) on Unix and OpenProce

fix(installer): stop codeg-mcp processes before upgrade

locked on Windows, breaking installer upgrades with "Error opening file
for writing: codeg-mcp.exe". On Linux/macOS overwriting a running binary
succeeds, but stale companions keep talking to the old inode and never
pick up the new logic.

- Bundle a Windows NSIS installer hook (PRE-INSTALL, PRE-UNINSTALL) that
  taskkills codeg-mcp.exe before the installer writes new

Skills with scripts/pyproject.toml had their .venv rebuilt lazily on the
first runtime `uv run`, leaking uv's "Building.../Installed" progress
(stderr) into the agent's chat and adding first-call latency that could
surface as "skill returned no data". Run `uv sync` right after rsync so
the venv is warm at sync time; build noise goes to the sync log. A uv
sync failure is logged as a warning and does not abort the sync.

fix(autoresearch): commit eval results per case (real 'database is locked' fix)

run_eval_suite committed only once, after the whole case loop. The per-case
eval_runs INSERTs therefore sat in one uncommitted transaction that held the
WAL write lock for the entire suite. Every per-draft write on another

fix(ci): rewrite deploy workflow in PowerShell for Windows runner

Replaces bash shell with pwsh throughout. On Windows with WSL installed,
`shell: bash` picks up system32\bash.exe (WSL) which fails on Windows
temp-file paths. Specifying a full Git Bash path causes Path.Combine()
to throw "Second path fragment must not be a drive or UNC name".
PowerShell is native on Windows runners and has no shell-resolution
ambiguity. All bash idioms (case, grep, for loops) rewritten in pwsh.
